- Contractor access to Customer PII is limited to a maximum of 90 days (CTL-02). `POL-014 §3.4`
- It may be renewed once, after re-approval. `POL-014 §3.4`
- The 90-day maximum replaced the previous 180-day maximum (POL-014 v2.1), per the postmortem for INC-2026-031. `INC-2026-031 §Actions`
- POL-022 also caps access to Restricted data at 90 days per approval, which is consistent with the PII limit. `POL-022 §3`

**Assumptions**
- Customer PII is treated as falling under the POL-014 contractor requirements; POL-022's Restricted data limit is cited only as corroboration.

- Access request records, including approvals, are retained for 7 years. `POL-030 §2. Retention schedule > Access request records (including approvals)`
- The Access Request and Approval Procedure defers to the Data Retention Policy (POL-030) for retention of these records. `PRC-012 §6`

- Payment card data is classified as Restricted. `POL-001 §3. Data category mapping > Payment card data`
- A system takes the highest classification of any data category it stores, so systems holding payment card data are Restricted (e.g., SYS-BILL Ledger Billing is listed as Restricted). `POL-001 §3` `REF-003 §System Inventory > SYS-BILL`
- Access to any system storing payment card data additionally requires Finance Systems Lead sign-off and completed PCI DSS training (CTL-10). `REF-005 §3`

- Access requests involving Restricted data must be approved or rejected within 5 business days. `PRC-012 §4`
- For comparison, standard requests (not involving Restricted data) have a 2 business day SLA. `PRC-012 §4`
- Privileged access to systems holding Restricted data also needs Security Governance approval in addition to standard approvals, which may be part of the approvals needed within the SLA. `POL-041 §2.3`

**Assumptions**
- Assumed 'approval SLA' refers to the PRC-012 service level for approving or rejecting requests.

**Gaps**
- The evidence does not say whether the 5 business day SLA applies when extra approvals such as Security Governance are required, or when the clock starts.

- Contractor access must be revoked within 24 hours of the engagement ending. `POL-022 §6`
- The sponsor must raise an offboarding ticket before the end date. `POL-022 §6`
- Contractor accounts must carry an end date matching the contract end date; the end date has been a mandatory field in Gatekeeper IAM since July 2026. `POL-022 §3` `REF-004 §Control Catalogue > CTL-02`
- Incident INC-2026-031 shows the rule was missed once: a Brightline Analytics contractor kept Atlas CRM read access for 47 days after the engagement ended. `INC-2026-031 §Summary`

- A just-in-time privileged access session can last a maximum of 8 hours. `POL-041 §2.2`
- The policy covers administrator, root and other privileged access to production systems. `POL-041 §1`
- All privileged sessions are recorded (CTL-06) and require MFA (CTL-01). `POL-041 §2.4`
- Separately, emergency access granted by Security Governance in a genuine operational emergency can last up to 24 hours; this is an emergency route, not a standard JIT session. `PRC-012 §7`

**Assumptions**
- The question refers to standard just-in-time privileged access to production systems under POL-041.
- The sponsor must raise the contractor onboarding ticket in Harbor Service Desk at least 5 business days before the contractor's start date. `PRC-007 §Onboarding`

- A vendor needs a completed security questionnaire. `VND-002 §2`
- A vendor also needs evidence of ISO/IEC 27001 certification or a SOC 2 Type II report, issued within the last 12 months. `VND-002 §2`
- An assessment is required for any vendor whose staff will access Confidential or Restricted data. `VND-002 §1`
- High-risk vendors additionally require Security Governance sign-off and an agreed remediation plan. `VND-002 §3`
- An assessment is valid for 12 months; once it expires, no new access can be granted until it is renewed. `VND-002 §3`
